question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -7\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 0 & a \\ ∗ & 1 & b \\ ∗ & 0 & c\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ find the value of $b+c.$
question.worked_solution:
Since the Jordan block $J$ has a single $3\times 3$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =-6,$ the columns of $P$ form the following chain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3}\overset{A+6I\,}{\to }{v}_{2}\overset{A+6I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A+6I\,}{\to }0\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that 

- the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvector ${v}_{1}$ of the eigenvalue $\lambda =-6,$

- the second column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ such that $(A+6I){v}_{2}={v}_{1},$

- the third column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{3}$ such that $(A+6I){v}_{3}={v}_{2}.$

Now, computing $A+6I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A+6I & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -7\end{aligned}]+6[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the matrix equation $(A+6I){v}_{3}={v}_{2}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have ${x}_{2}=2-{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
-{x}_{1}+(2-{x}_{3})+{x}_{3}=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=1.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2-{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=0,$ we get  

$$
{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $b+c=2+0=2.$
